entries.summary: clearDeviceEnrollment and Daemon.unpair() no longer delete another store's credential or staged first pairing under the same productId: they hold a per-user productId lock from validation through deletion, and pairing takes it across its credential writes, each waiting up to 30 seconds. FirstPairingAttempt gains storeIdentity (DeviceStore.identity, the SHA-256 hex of the resolved storeDir); an injected DeviceCredentialBackend keeps every attempt field, or the store's own attempt is refused. A clear refuses another store's attempt as store_not_bound and an attempt that names no store (staged by 0.42.0) with the new DeviceEnrollmentClearErrorCode pairing_attempt_unattributed; clearDeviceEnrollment({ ..., clearUnattributedAttempt: true }) deletes it. Pairing applies the same rule (#2033): it reuses only its own store's staged attempt and otherwise throws the new FirstPairingAttemptRefusedError (store_not_bound, which replaceOtherStore discards, or pairing_attempt_unattributed). A running daemon's token renewal takes the same lock around its write and writes only while the OS entry still holds its store's enrollment; otherwise the daemon halts as store_not_bound or re_pair_required (#2034). No holder keeps the lock across a network request. BlobClient and InstallSkillPacksOptions change only through the types they reference (#1964).
